PLAN OF DISSOLUTION AND WINDING UP

Alderbrook Instruments, Inc.
A Delaware corporation
Adopted by the Board of Directors on June 2, 2026
Approved by the Stockholders on June 26, 2026

1. ADOPTION AND EFFECTIVENESS

The Board of Directors of Alderbrook Instruments, Inc. (the "Company") has determined that it is advisable and in the best interests of the Company and its stockholders to dissolve the Company, and has adopted this Plan of Dissolution and Winding Up (this "Plan") and directed that it be submitted to the stockholders. The stockholders approved the dissolution and this Plan by the affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the outstanding stock entitled to vote, as section 275 of the General Corporation Law of the State of Delaware requires. This Plan becomes effective on the filing of a Certificate of Dissolution with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware (the "Effective Date").

2. CERTIFICATE OF DISSOLUTION

As soon as practicable after stockholder approval, and after payment or provision for payment of the Company's franchise taxes as section 277 requires, the officers shall file a Certificate of Dissolution with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware.

3. CONTINUED EXISTENCE

Under section 278, the Company continues in existence for three years after the Effective Date, and for such longer period as the Court of Chancery directs, for the purpose of prosecuting and defending suits, settling and closing its business, disposing of its property, discharging its liabilities, and distributing to its stockholders any remaining assets. The Company shall not continue the business for which it was organized.

4. WINDING UP

4.1 Cessation of Operations. The Company shall cease conducting its business except as necessary to wind up.

4.2 Collection of Assets. The officers shall collect all accounts receivable, terminate all leases and contracts on the most favorable terms reasonably available, and reduce the Company's non-cash assets to cash or cash equivalents through sale, assignment, or abandonment.

4.3 Employees. The Company shall terminate the employment of its employees on the schedule the Board approves, shall pay all accrued wages, commissions, and accrued vacation as Delaware law requires, and shall provide any notice required by the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act.

4.4 Books and Records. The Company shall preserve its books and records for seven years after the Effective Date, and shall designate an officer or an agent as custodian.

5. NOTICE TO CLAIMANTS AND PROVISION FOR CLAIMS

5.1 Election of Procedure. The Company elects to follow the court-supervised procedure of sections 280 and 281(a), rather than the alternative procedure of section 281(b).

5.2 Notice. The Company shall give notice of the dissolution to all persons having a claim against it, other than a claim in a pending action, by mail to the last known address of each claimant and by publication once each week for two consecutive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation in the county of its registered office, stating that the claim must be presented in writing with reasonable particularity, the mailing address to which it must be sent, and that the claim will be barred if not received by the date stated, which shall be not less than sixty days after the notice.

5.3 Rejection. The Company shall reject in whole or in part any claim it determines not to be valid, by written notice mailed to the claimant, stating that the claim will be barred if an action is not commenced within ninety days after the rejection.

5.4 Security for Contingent Claims. The Company shall offer security for any contingent, conditional, or unmatured contractual claim, and shall petition the Court of Chancery to determine the amount and form of security reasonably likely to be sufficient for claims that are the subject of a pending action, and for unknown claims that may arise within five years after the Effective Date.

5.5 Payment. The Company shall pay all claims made and not rejected, post all security offered and not rejected, and post any security ordered by the Court of Chancery.

6. DISTRIBUTIONS

6.1 Priority. After payment or provision for payment of all claims under Section 5, the Company shall distribute its remaining assets to its stockholders in accordance with the liquidation preferences in its Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation: first to the holders of Series B Preferred Stock, then to the holders of Series A Preferred Stock, and thereafter to the holders of Common Stock.

6.2 Liquidating Distributions. The Board may make one or more liquidating distributions in cash or in kind, and may establish a reserve for expenses and contingent liabilities. Any amount remaining in the reserve after the reserve is no longer required shall be distributed on the same priority.

6.3 Liquidating Trust. If the Board determines it is advisable, the Company may transfer its remaining assets and liabilities to a liquidating trust for the benefit of the stockholders, and the transfer shall be treated as a distribution to the stockholders followed by a contribution to the trust.

6.4 Unclaimed Distributions. Any distribution unclaimed after one year shall be delivered to the state of the stockholder's last known address as unclaimed property under that state's escheat law.

7. TAX MATTERS

The Company shall file a Form 966 with the Internal Revenue Service within thirty days after the adoption of this Plan, shall file all final federal, state, and local tax returns, and shall issue Forms 1099-DIV reporting liquidating distributions. The Company shall not make any distribution to stockholders before it has paid or provided for its tax liabilities.

8. INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE

The Company shall continue to indemnify its directors, officers, employees, and agents to the fullest extent its Certificate of Incorporation, its Bylaws, and Delaware law permit, for acts and omissions occurring before and during the winding up, and shall purchase a six-year runoff endorsement to its directors and officers liability policy before the final distribution.

9. AUTHORITY OF OFFICERS

The officers are authorized and directed to take any action, and to execute and deliver any instrument, that they determine necessary or advisable to carry out this Plan, including the filing of the Certificate of Dissolution, the sale or abandonment of assets, the settlement of claims, and the making of distributions, without further stockholder action.

10. AMENDMENT AND ABANDONMENT

The Board may amend this Plan, and may abandon the dissolution before the Certificate of Dissolution is filed, without further stockholder action. After the Certificate of Dissolution is filed, the dissolution may be revoked only as section 311 permits.
